## Q1
For sending input I₆ to the output line of an 8×1 multiplexer, which selection-line combination is required?

## Q1 - Options
(A) 001
(B) 100
(C) 110
(D) 111

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q34

An 8-to-1 multiplexer uses three select bits to encode the input index in binary. Since 6 in binary is 110, the select lines S₂S₁S₀ must be 110; 111 would instead select I₇.

## Q4
Which IC family has the lowest power consumption?

## Q4 - Options
(A) ECL
(B) MOS
(C) TTL
(D) CMOS

## Q4 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 2 · Q73

CMOS has very low static power consumption because its complementary transistor pair ideally draws significant current only while switching. ECL and TTL consume substantially more steady power.

## Q6
What is the Gray-code equivalent of decimal 8?

## Q6 - Options
(A) 1000
(B) 1100
(C) 1010
(D) 1110

## Q6 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q9

Decimal 8 is binary 1000. Gray code is found by XORing the binary number with itself shifted right one bit: 1000 XOR 0100 = 1100.

## Q7
Which gate does not output 1 when both inputs are 0?

## Q7 - Options
(A) NAND and NOR only
(B) NOR and XOR only
(C) XOR and XNOR only
(D) XOR only

## Q7 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2025 (26 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q59

At inputs 0 and 0, NAND outputs 1, NOR outputs 1, and XNOR outputs 1 because the inputs match. XOR alone outputs 0, so it is the only listed gate that does not output 1.

## Q9
Consider the given number (45) y where y is the base of the number. Some of the possible values of y are given below.<br>
A. 5<br>
B. 6<br>
C. 7<br>
D. 8

## Q9 - Options
(A) (A), (B) and (C) Only
(B) (B), (C) and (D) Only
(C) (A), (C) and (D) Only
(D) (A), (B), (C) and (D)

## Q9 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q11

In base y every digit used must be smaller than y. The numeral 45 uses the digit 5, so y must exceed 5. Base 5 is therefore invalid, while bases 6, 7 and 8 all admit the digits 4 and 5. The valid values are (B), (C) and (D) — option B.

## Q11
Consider the following statements regarding combinational and sequential circuits.<br>
A. Output of combinational circuits depends on the only current input.<br>
B. Output of combinational circuit depends on the both current input and previous output.<br>
C. Output of sequential circuit depends on the current input.<br>
D. Output of sequential circuit depends on both current input and previous output.

## Q11 - Options
(A) (A) and (C) Only
(B) (A) and (D) Only
(C) (B) and (D) Only
(D) (B) and (C) Only

## Q11 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q40

A combinational circuit’s output is a pure function of its present inputs, which makes (A) true and (B) false. A sequential circuit adds memory, so its output depends on both the present input and the stored previous state, making (D) true and (C) false. Only (A) and (D) — option B.

## Q12
Match List-I with List-II.

| List-I (Counter) | List-II (uses/working) |
|---|---|
| (A) N-bit Ring Counter | (I) Uses universal clock |
| (B) Synchronous Counter | (II) Counts exactly N states |
| (C) Asynchronous Counter | (III) Counts 0 to 9 |
| (D) Decimal Counter | (IV) Main clock is applied to first flip-flop only |

## Q12 - Options
(A) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
(B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
(C) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
(D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)

## Q12 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Aug 2024 (23 Aug, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q53

An N-bit ring counter cycles through exactly N states, so (A)-(II). A synchronous counter clocks every flip-flop from one common clock, giving (B)-(I). In an asynchronous (ripple) counter only the first flip-flop sees the main clock, so (C)-(IV). A decimal counter counts 0 to 9, so (D)-(III). Option C is correct.

## Q15
What is the (4 + 4) bit binary fixed point equivalent of -(3.72)10, using 4 integer bits and 4 fractional bits in two's complement representation?

## Q15 - Options
(A) 0011.1100
(B) 0011.1010
(C) 1100.0100
(D) 0011.1011

## Q15 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2023 (17 Jun, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q80

Converting -(3.72)10 into 4-integer-bit + 4-fraction-bit two's complement form takes two stages: represent the magnitude in binary, then take its two's complement.

Integer part: 3 in 4 bits is 0011.

Fractional part: 0.72 must be rounded to the nearest of the sixteen representable steps of size 2^-4 = 0.0625. Since 0.72 / 0.0625 = 11.52, the nearest step is 12, and 12 in 4 bits is 1100, representing 0.75.

So the magnitude 3.72 rounds to the representation 0011.1100.

Two's complement of the magnitude: invert every bit of 0011.1100 to get 1100.0011, then add 1 at the least significant fractional position (weight 2^-4):<br>
1100.0011 + 0000.0001 = 1100.0100

So -(3.72)10 in this 4.4 two's complement format is 1100.0100. Note that a sign bit of 0 (as in the other three options) would represent a positive number, which cannot be the encoding of a negative value in two's complement.

## Q16
In 16-bit 2's Complementation representation, the decimal number -28 is

## Q16 - Options
(A) 1111 1111 0001 1100
(B) 1111 1111 1111 0100
(C) 1111 1111 1110 0100
(D) 1111 1111 1110 0011

## Q16 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Combinational/Sequential Circuits, Flip-Flops & Number Systems
**Source:** UGC NET Mar 2023 (15 Mar, Shift 1) · Paper 2 · Q5

To find the 2's complement of -28 in 16 bits, first write +28 in binary, then invert every bit and add 1.

28 in 16-bit binary is 0000 0000 0001 1100

Inverting every bit (1's complement) gives 1111 1111 1110 0011, and adding 1 gives 1111 1111 1110 0100

Option D is the 1's complement of 28, not the final 2's complement, and options A and B do not match either the inversion or the addition step correctly.
